knowledgePoint.zh: 梯度下降算法——网络如何通过逐步调整权重来学习
knowledgePoint.en: The gradient descent algorithm — how networks learn by gradually adjusting weights

recallIntro.zh: 你闭上眼，又回到了那间教室。鲁梅尔哈特教授站在白板前，画了一片起伏的丘陵地形。他在最高的山峰上画了一个小人，然后用红笔在小人的眼睛上画了一条横线——「蒙住了。」他笑着说。
recallIntro.en: You close your eyes and find yourself back in that classroom. Prof. Rumelhart stands at the whiteboard, drawing a hilly terrain. He draws a small figure on the highest peak, then draws a red line across the figure's eyes — 「Blindfolded」. He says with a smile.

recallOutro.zh: 你回过神来。那片起伏的丘陵仍在脑海中浮现——蒙着眼的登山者，试探着脚下的坡度，小心翼翼地往低处走。梯度下降，原来就是这样一种朴素而有效的策略。
recallOutro.en: You return to the present. That hilly terrain still lingers in your mind — the blindfolded hiker, feeling the slope underfoot, carefully stepping downhill. Gradient descent, such a simple yet effective strategy.

text.zh: 鲁梅尔哈特教授今天进来的时候，手上没有胶片——而是拎着一个网球。他把网球放在讲台上，轻轻推了一下。网球沿着微微倾斜的桌面滚动，最终停在了桌子的最低角落。他看着网球停下来的位置，满意地笑了。
text.en: Prof. Rumelhart walks in today without transparencies — instead, he's carrying a tennis ball. He places it on the lectern and gives it a gentle push. The ball rolls along the slightly tilted surface and comes to rest at the lowest corner. He looks at where the ball stopped and smiles with satisfaction.

text.zh: 看到了吗？网球自然地滚向了最低点。它不需要知道整个桌面的形状——它只需要感受当前位置的倾斜方向，然后朝着下坡方向移动。这就是{梯度下降}最直观的比喻。
text.en: See that? The tennis ball naturally rolled to the lowest point. It didn't need to know the shape of the entire surface — it only needed to feel the slope at its current position and move downhill. That's the most intuitive metaphor for {gradient descent}.

text.zh: 上节课我们学了反向传播——它告诉我们每个{权重}应该朝哪个方向调整。但「朝哪个方向」只是问题的一半。另一半是：每一步该走多远？这就是梯度下降要回答的问题。
text.en: Last lesson we learned backpropagation — it tells us which direction each {weight} should be adjusted. But 「which direction」 is only half the problem. The other half is: how far should each step be? That's the question gradient descent answers.

text.zh: 让我给你们画一个更完整的画面。想象你被蒙上了双眼，站在一片起伏不平的丘陵地带。你的目标是找到最低的山谷。你看不见周围的地形，唯一能做的就是用脚感受当前位置的坡度——哪个方向是往下的？坡度有多陡？
text.en: Let me paint a fuller picture. Imagine you're blindfolded, standing in hilly terrain. Your goal is to find the lowest valley. You can't see the terrain around you; all you can do is feel the slope under your feet — which direction goes downhill? How steep is the slope?

text.zh: 你的策略很简单：每一步都朝最陡的下坡方向走。坡度越陡，说明你离谷底还远，步子可以大一些；坡度越平缓，说明快到谷底了，步子应该小一些。这就是梯度下降——「梯度」是坡度的数学表达，「下降」是你的行走方向。
text.en: Your strategy is simple: at each step, walk in the steepest downhill direction. The steeper the slope, the farther you probably are from the bottom, so your steps can be bigger; the gentler the slope, the closer you are, so your steps should be smaller. This is gradient descent — 「gradient」 is the mathematical expression for slope, 「descent」 is your direction of travel.

text.zh: 在神经网络中，那片丘陵就是「误差曲面」——每一个点代表一组特定的权重值，而这个点的高度代表在那组权重下网络的误差大小。我们要做的是找到误差最小的那个点。而{学习率}决定了我们每一步「走多远」。
text.en: In a neural network, that hilly terrain is the 「error surface」 — each point represents a specific set of weight values, and the height at that point represents the network's error with those weights. Our goal is to find the point where the error is smallest. And the {learning rate} determines 「how far」 we step each time.

text.zh: 学习率太大会怎样？想象你在山坡上迈了一大步，结果一脚跨过了山谷，落在了对面的山坡上。下一步你又迈回来，又跨过了谷底。你在山谷两侧来回弹跳，永远落不到谷底——甚至可能越弹越高，完全失控。
text.en: What happens if the learning rate is too large? Imagine you take a huge step on the hillside, and you overshoot the valley entirely, landing on the opposite slope. Your next step bounces you back, overshooting again. You bounce back and forth across the valley, never reaching the bottom — and you might even bounce higher and higher, completely out of control.

text.zh: 学习率太小呢？你每一步只挪动一点点。方向是对的，但速度太慢了——也许你要走上一百万步才能到达谷底。在实际训练中，这意味着等待数周甚至数月。而且更糟糕的是，你可能在某个浅浅的凹陷处就停下了，以为那就是谷底。
text.en: What if the learning rate is too small? You inch forward with each step. The direction is right, but the speed is painfully slow — maybe you'd need a million steps to reach the bottom. In practice, this means waiting weeks or even months. And worse, you might stop at some shallow depression, thinking it's the valley floor.

text.zh: 如果学习率设得太大，训练过程中最可能出现什么现象？
text.en: If the learning rate is set too large, what is most likely to happen during training?

text.zh: 误差来回震荡，无法稳定下降，甚至可能越来越大
text.en: The error oscillates back and forth, unable to decrease steadily, and may even grow larger

text.zh: 完全正确。大步长导致在最优解附近反复跳跃，每一步都跨过了谷底。如果步子太大，你甚至会「弹射」到更高的误差区域——网络不但没有学好，反而越学越差。这在实践中是一个非常常见的问题。
text.en: Exactly right. Large step sizes cause repeated leaping around the optimum, overshooting the valley floor each time. If the steps are too large, you might even 「catapult」 into higher error regions — the network not only fails to learn but actually gets worse. This is a very common problem in practice.

text.zh: 训练会更快收敛到最优解
text.en: Training would converge to the optimum more quickly

text.zh: 直觉上「步子大就走得快」似乎说得通，但实际上恰恰相反。想象你在走钢丝——跨大步不会让你更快到达终点，只会让你更容易摔下来。太大的学习率会导致权重更新过度，误差来回震荡甚至发散。适度才是关键。
text.en: Intuitively 「bigger steps means faster progress」 seems to make sense, but in reality it's the opposite. Imagine you're walking a tightrope — taking big steps won't get you to the end faster, it'll just make you more likely to fall. Too large a learning rate causes excessive weight updates, making the error oscillate or even diverge. Moderation is key.

text.zh: 可能跳过局部最优，但也可能跳过全局最优
text.en: Might skip over local optima, but could also skip the global optimum

text.zh: 这个回答展示了很好的两面思维。确实，大的学习率偶尔能帮你跳出局部陷阱——但这是不可控的。你无法预测它会跳到更好的位置还是更差的位置。主要的危险是，过大的步长会导致误差来回震荡甚至不断增大。可控性比冒险更重要。
text.en: This answer shows great two-sided thinking. Indeed, a large learning rate can occasionally help you escape local traps — but it's uncontrollable. You can't predict whether it'll jump to a better or worse position. The main danger is that oversized steps cause the error to oscillate or keep growing. Controllability matters more than risk-taking.

text.zh: 选择合适的学习率更像是一门手艺而非科学。太大会震荡，太小会停滞。在实践中，我们通常从一个适中的值开始，观察误差的变化趋势，然后凭经验做调整。目前还没有一个万能的公式来告诉你最佳学习率是多少。
text.en: Choosing the right learning rate is more of a craft than a science. Too large and you oscillate, too small and you stagnate. In practice, we usually start with a moderate value, observe how the error changes, and adjust based on experience. There isn't yet a universal formula to tell you the optimal learning rate.

text.zh: 现在来说一个更深层的问题。记得那片丘陵吗？它不只有一个山谷——可能有很多个。有些山谷很深，有些很浅。你蒙着眼走下坡路，最终停在了一个谷底。但你怎么知道这是最深的那个山谷？
text.en: Now let me address a deeper issue. Remember that hilly terrain? It doesn't have just one valley — there could be many. Some valleys are deep, some shallow. You walk downhill blindfolded and eventually stop at a valley floor. But how do you know this is the deepest valley?

text.zh: 你不知道。这就是「局部最小值」和「全局最小值」的区别。梯度下降只能保证你找到一个往四周都是上坡的点——但它可能只是附近区域的最低点，整个地形中可能还有更低的地方。
text.en: You don't. This is the difference between a 「local minimum」 and the 「global minimum」. Gradient descent can only guarantee you find a point where the slope goes uphill in every direction — but it might only be the lowest point in the nearby area. There could be lower points elsewhere in the entire landscape.

text.zh: 梯度下降能保证找到全局最优解吗？
text.en: Can gradient descent guarantee finding the global optimum?

text.zh: 不能——蒙着眼走下坡只能到达某个局部最低点，无法保证是全局最低
text.en: No — walking downhill blindfolded can only reach some local minimum, with no guarantee it's the global one

text.zh: 正确。对于大多数复杂问题，误差曲面有无数个局部最小值，梯度下降只能保证你到达其中一个。但有一个实践中的好消息：对于很多实际问题，那些局部最小值的误差其实差不多。也就是说，虽然你找不到「最好的」，但你找到的通常已经「足够好」了。
text.en: Correct. For most complex problems, the error surface has countless local minima, and gradient descent can only guarantee reaching one of them. But here's the good news in practice: for many real problems, those local minima tend to have similar error values. In other words, even though you can't find 「the best」, what you find is usually 「good enough」.

text.zh: 取决于学习率和起始位置——运气好的话也许可以
text.en: Depends on the learning rate and starting position — with luck, maybe

text.zh: 你说的因素确实有影响——不同的起始位置会导致不同的终点，学习率也会影响路径。但即使考虑了这些因素，我们仍然没有理论上的保证。这就是为什么在实践中，我们有时会用不同的随机起始点训练多次，然后选择结果最好的那一次。这是一种务实的策略，但不是数学意义上的保证。
text.en: The factors you mention do have an impact — different starting positions lead to different endpoints, and learning rate affects the path too. But even accounting for these factors, we still don't have a theoretical guarantee. That's why in practice, we sometimes train multiple times with different random starting points and pick the best result. It's a pragmatic strategy, not a mathematical guarantee.

text.zh: 如果训练足够久，应该能遍历整个空间最终找到
text.en: If we train long enough, it should be able to explore the entire space and eventually find it

text.zh: 这是一个常见的误解。梯度下降并非随机搜索，它始终沿着下坡方向前进。一旦落入一个山谷，它只会在谷底附近徘徊，不会突然跳到另一个山谷。训练得再久，也改变不了这一点。它就像一条河流，水总是往低处流，不会自己爬上对面的山坡，再去探索另一片谷地。
text.en: That's a common misconception. Gradient descent isn't random search — it always follows the downhill direction. Once it falls into a valley, it only circles near the bottom; it won't suddenly jump to another valley. No amount of additional training changes this. It's like a river — water always flows downhill; it won't climb up the opposite slope to explore another valley on its own.

text.zh: 局部最小值是梯度下降最大的理论弱点。但让我告诉你一件奇妙的事情——在实践中，反向传播加上梯度下降的效果比理论预期的要好得多。我们的PDP网络在很多任务上都表现出色，尽管我们无法证明找到了最优解。有时候，「足够好」已经是了不起的成就。
text.en: Local minima are gradient descent's biggest theoretical weakness. But let me tell you something wonderful — in practice, backpropagation plus gradient descent works much better than theory would predict. Our PDP networks perform excellently on many tasks, even though we can't prove we've found the optimal solution. Sometimes, 「good enough」 is already a remarkable achievement.

suggestedContent.zh: 梯度下降的核心思想：蒙眼在误差曲面上寻找最低点，每一步朝最陡下坡方向走。学习率控制步长——太大会震荡，太小会停滞。理论上无法保证找到全局最优，但实践中「足够好」的解已经非常有用。
suggestedContent.en: Core idea of gradient descent: blindfolded search for the lowest point on the error surface, stepping in the steepest downhill direction each time. Learning rate controls step size — too large causes oscillation, too small causes stagnation. No theoretical guarantee of finding global optimum, but 「good enough」 solutions are already very useful in practice.

text.zh: 梯度下降既美妙又让人沮丧。美妙在于它的简洁，只需要两样东西：当前的梯度和学习率。沮丧在于它的盲目，你永远不知道全局地形长什么样，只能感受脚下的坡度。但也许这正是它的力量所在：不需要上帝视角，从局部信息出发就能一步步改善。
text.en: Gradient descent is both beautiful and frustrating. Beautiful in its simplicity — it needs only two things: the current gradient and the learning rate. Frustrating in its blindness — you never know what the global terrain looks like; you can only feel the slope under your feet. But perhaps that's precisely its strength: no need for a god's-eye view; you can improve step by step starting from local information alone.

text.zh: 梯度下降「只能看到脚下的坡度」——你觉得这是优势还是劣势？
text.en: Gradient descent 「can only see the slope under its feet」 — do you see this as an advantage or a disadvantage?

text.zh: 优势——不需要知道全局信息就能工作，计算成本低
text.en: Advantage — it works without needing global information, with low computational cost

text.zh: 这一点非常重要。如果你需要了解整个误差曲面才能做出一步，那对于有几千个权重的网络来说，计算量是不可想象的。梯度下降的局部性让它在实践中可行——你只需要当前位置的信息就能前进。这种「从局部到全局」的策略，在很多领域都是有效的。
text.en: This is extremely important. If you needed to understand the entire error surface to take one step, for networks with thousands of weights, the computation would be unimaginable. Gradient descent's locality makes it practically feasible — you only need information at your current position to move forward. This 「local to global」 strategy is effective in many fields.

text.zh: 劣势——容易被困在局部最优解，看不到更好的可能
text.en: Disadvantage — easily trapped in local optima, unable to see better possibilities

text.zh: 这确实是梯度下降最为人诟病的缺陷。如果你落入了一个浅坑，你可能永远不知道旁边还有一个深谷。但有趣的是，当网络足够大、维度足够高的时候，局部最小值的数量虽然增多了，但它们之间的差异反而缩小了。高维空间有一些反直觉的特性——这个话题以后有机会再展开。
text.en: This is indeed gradient descent's most criticized flaw. If you fall into a shallow pit, you might never know there's a deep valley right next door. But interestingly, when the network is large enough and the dimensions high enough, although local minima multiply, the differences between them actually shrink. High-dimensional spaces have some counterintuitive properties — a topic for another time.

text.zh: 两者兼有——正是这种局限性让它实用，也让它不完美
text.en: Both — it's precisely this limitation that makes it practical and also imperfect

text.zh: （微笑）这也许是最成熟的回答。工程中的很多工具都有这种特点——它的优势和劣势来自同一个源头。局部性让它快速、实用，同时也让它盲目、容易被困。接受这种权衡，然后想办法缓解劣势。这就是研究者的日常工作。
text.en: (Smiles) That may be the most mature answer. Many engineering tools share this characteristic — their strengths and weaknesses come from the same source. Locality makes it fast and practical, while also making it blind and prone to getting trapped. Accepting this trade-off and finding ways to mitigate the downsides — that's a researcher's daily work.

text.zh: 现在我们有了两件工具：反向传播告诉我们方向，梯度下降带着我们前进。下节课，我们要回到那个让神经网络跌入寒冬的问题——XOR。我要亲手向你们展示，一个多层网络如何解决单层网络无法解决的难题。隐藏层的力量，远超你们的想象。
text.en: Now we have two tools: backpropagation tells us the direction, gradient descent carries us forward. Next lesson, we'll return to the problem that sent neural networks into winter — XOR. I'm going to show you firsthand how a multi-layer network solves what a single-layer network cannot. The power of hidden layers is far beyond what you might imagine.

suggestedContent.zh: 梯度下降的权衡：局部性既是优势也是劣势。学习率是关键超参数——调参更像手艺而非科学。局部最小值问题理论上无法避免，但实践中多数局部最优解已经「足够好」。
suggestedContent.en: The trade-off of gradient descent: locality is both advantage and weakness. Learning rate is the key hyperparameter — tuning it is more craft than science. Local minima can't be theoretically avoided, but in practice most local optima are already 「good enough」.

text.zh: 鲁梅尔哈特教授拿起讲台上的网球，在手里抛了一下。「有趣的是，」他在门口停了一下，「大自然也不需要上帝视角来优化——进化也是一种局部搜索，一代一代地试探，却创造了整个生物圈。也许梯度下降的盲目，恰恰是它最像自然的地方。」他挥了挥手，走出了教室。
text.en: Prof. Rumelhart picks up the tennis ball from the lectern and tosses it once. 「Interestingly,」  he pauses at the door, 「nature doesn't need a god's-eye view for optimization either — evolution is also a local search, probing generation by generation, yet it created the entire biosphere. Perhaps gradient descent's blindness is precisely what makes it most like nature」. He waves and walks out of the classroom.
